heard: A single storm on Saturn can wrap around the entire planet. Most people think Jupiter has the solar system's only megastorms, but Saturn hides a secret. Every 30 years, the gas giant erupts with a colossal great white spot. Six of these planetary tempests have been recorded since 1876. In 2010, NASA's Cassini spacecraft watched a stormhead grow as wide as Earth. This monster generated 10 lightning flashes per second while whipping out a massive tail. Within six months, that tail stretched around the world until it hit its own head. These massive chemical remnants linger in the upper atmosphere for centuries, leaving permanent scars until Saturn unleashes its next planetary monster.
